decision_rationale: Skill: stem asks 'which development' a historian would point to — identifying the development, not explicating it (1.A; recheck). Topic: the driver is a corporate/economic choice by multinational food firms, not a technological advance — 9.4 Economics in the Global Age (recheck).

Topic: the item is inherently a comparison of two commemorative state practices (5.A skill); 1.7 Comparison in the Period is the comparison-oriented topic. 1.1 (Song-era East Asia) has no connection to the content (first).

Topic: Tocqueville's 1835 Manchester passage describes industrial-urban society conditions, which is 5.9 Society and the Industrial Age. 5.3 (Industrial Revolution Begins) covers origins in England, not the passage's subject (first).

Skill: stem asks what the cartoon reveals/can be used to show — identifying the cartoonist's point of view (gendered mockery), not judging a limit on its use, so 2.A (recheck). Topic: 1791 Catherine the Great/enlightened-despot context is 5.1 The Enlightenment, not 5.2 nationalism/revolutions (recheck).

Skill: 'could best use this regulation to study' asks what the source reveals about its own historical situation (a Christian municipal authority imposing social boundaries) — identifying historical situation, 2.A. 2.C requires a significance/limitation judgment the stem does not ask for (recheck).

Topic: Guillén's poem is a post-independence Latin American identity/heritage work (three-roots ancestry). 8.6 Newly Independent States is the least-bad fit; 8.7 (Global Resistance to Established Order) is about resistance movements, not heritage identity (first).

Skill: stem moves from the specific (Cerro Rico) to asking which broader development it was central to — identifying/describing the historical context for the specific, which is 4.A. 4.B would require explaining how the specific is situated; here the context itself is what must be identified (first).

Skill: stem asks for the most plausible explanation of the war's neglect — explaining the specific development by situating it within the broader context of American anti-colonial national memory. The 'why' demands explanation, 4.B (recheck).

Skill: 'would most usefully pair these two images to illustrate' asks the student to identify/describe the broader historical context the sources illustrate (Cold War technological rivalry) — identification of context, 4.A, not an explanation of situatedness (first).

Skill: 'complicates that argument by' asks how Schmidel's evidence qualifies/modifies the disease thesis — corroborate/qualify/modify with alternative evidence, 6.D, not merely explaining relationships among evidence pieces (first). Topic: Spanish conquest/gunfire in the Americas is empire establishment, 4.4; 4.2 is about causes of exploration voyages (first).

Skill: the classification 'intensive' is given in the stem; the student must explain WHY chinampas qualify (high yields, labor, lakebed fertilizer) — explaining a historical concept, 1.B (recheck). Topic: not comparative, so 3.4 is wrong; the Aztec/Mexica imperial context in 1450-1750 best fits 3.1 Empires Expand as the least-bad unit-3 option (recheck).

Skill: 'the table as a whole most clearly undermines which claim?' uses the data as evidence to refute a claim — qualifying/modifying an argument with diverse evidence, 6.D. 6.C is about explaining relationships among evidence pieces, not claim-refutation (first).

Topic: the passage describes Tokugawa social hierarchy (shi-no-ko-sho) as a method of imperial social administration/legitimacy, which is 3.2 Empires: Administration. 3.1 (Empires Expand) is about expansion, not social order (recheck).

Topic: the stem is explicitly comparative (yasak most closely resembles which system — the encomienda), matching 3.4 Comparison in Land-Based Empires. 3.1 (Empires Expand) misses the comparative task (first).

Topic: negritude's challenge to the French assimilation doctrine is part of the post-1900 challenge to colonial power. Constrained to unit 7, 7.1 Shifting Power After 1900 is the least-bad fit; 7.5 is about post-WWI unresolved tensions (Versailles, fascism) and has no colonial content (first).

Topic: the stem describes what nonalignment meant in practice for newly independent states (Sukarno, Nkrumah, Nasser playing both sides) — the item is about the behavior of newly independent states, 8.6, not Cold War structure itself, 8.2 (recheck).

Skill: 'what does this best illustrate about Hellenistic cultural exchange?' asks the student to identify the process shown (conquered peoples adapting Greek forms) — identification, 1.A, not explication of a concept (recheck).
Skill: 'what was the fundamental reason' the Americas were isolated asks the student to identify the cause of a historical condition — identification, 1.A (recheck).

Skill: 'historians also credit the Pax Mongolica. With what?' asks the student to identify the development credited (secure trade routes) — identification, 1.A (first). Topic: constrained to unit 1, the Mongol/East-Asian imperial context fits 1.1 Developments in East Asia better than the comparison topic 1.7 (first).
Skill: 'for which reason' the potato drove population growth asks for the causal account (calories per acre on poor soils) — explaining a historical development, 1.B (recheck).

Skill: 'in which belief' deists differed asks the student to identify the distinguishing belief (clockmaker God) — identification, 1.A, not explication of deism as a concept (first). Topic: Enlightenment thought does not belong in unit 4 at all; 4.1 (Technological Innovations) is clearly wrong, so 4.8 Continuity and Change stands as the least-bad generic unit-4 bucket (recheck).

Topic: Ottoman reception of expelled Jews as pragmatic tolerance of useful minorities in a multi-religious empire is squarely 4.7 Changing Social Hierarchies (minority status in empires). 4.8 is not a content topic (first).

Skill: 'best reflects which priority' asks the student to identify the priority (industrial/military strength to resist the West) — identification, 1.A (first). Topic: the slogan reflects the Meiji government's role in driving industrialization — 5.6 Industrialization: Government's Role, not 5.4 (first).
Topic: treaty ports — extraterritoriality and treaty-fixed tariffs without direct colonial control — is economic imperialism, 6.5, not territorial state expansion, 6.2 (recheck).
Topic: the invasion of Poland directly caused the outbreak of WWII (Britain/France declaring war) — this is the cause of the war, 7.6 Causes of World War II, not its conduct, 7.7 (recheck).
